A1.justification: Both PDFs describe RV-HATE. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching material moved between the main text and appendices.

before.justification: v1 reports original experiments on five datasets, including baseline comparisons, module ablations, error analyses, and embedding visualizations.

after.justification: v2 retains those original empirical results and adds reported training-time and inference-latency comparisons in Table 5.

M1.justification: The four modules, contrastive-learning procedures, and PPO-guided soft voting remain unchanged. New Appendix H documents the policy-network architecture without reporting a change to the procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use IHC, SBIC, DYNA, Hateval, and Toxigen for the same detection tasks, including only English Hateval data. The added timing evaluation uses the existing IHC dataset.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains CE, SCL, SharedCon, and LAHN; Figure 5 retains SharedCon. The new efficiency table reuses SharedCon and LAHN. Newly discussed related methods are not added as evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Table 5 introduces an efficiency evaluation covering parameter counts, training time measured on IHC, and inference latency. Existing dataset splits, six-epoch training budgets, hyperparameter choices, and macro-F1 evaluation remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New Section 5.5 examines the computational overhead of the four-module ensemble relative to encoder baselines. Existing ablations, error analyses, confusion matrices, and embedding analyses are retained; consolidating error tables adds no new error-analysis evidence.

E5.justification: Three-seed averaging and the standard deviations reported in Table 2 are unchanged. No new significance test, confidence interval, or uncertainty-estimation procedure is specified.

E6.justification: New Table 5 reports approximately one hour of training per encoder, 5–10 additional minutes for PPO, and 0.5–1.5 ms inference latency per encoder, multiplied by four for RV-HATE. Matched benchmark scores, ablation values, error ratios, voting weights, and plotted results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The soft-voting expressions, PPO objective, and Appendix G IQR equations are unchanged. No theorem, proof, substantive derivation, or formal assumption is added or revised.

C1.justification: Both versions claim improved detection through dataset-specific module weighting and interpretable module contributions, retaining the average 1.8-percentage-point advantage. The new contribution bullets summarize existing claims.

C2.justification: Section 5.5 newly discusses parallel training, small PPO overhead, and the four-pass inference cost as an efficiency tradeoff. Section 6 also drops v1's explicit error-sample qualification when describing Toxigen's absence of broken sentences. The stated limitations otherwise remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix H newly specifies the four-dimensional policy input, two-layer feature extractor with hidden dimension 64, actor and critic heads, and component parameter counts. Section 5.5 adds runtime information. These are disclosures; the existing implementation settings and code-access statement are retained.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds CONELA (Kim et al., 2025), AmpleHate (Lee et al., 2025), and a Lee et al. (2018) citation, while removing Ghosh et al. (2023), Rawat et al. (2024), and Xie et al. (2024). The broader research positioning remains stable.

P1.justification: v2 adds contribution bullets, edits selected paragraphs and the conclusion, corrects the Section 3 title, and moves error-analysis discussion into Section 6. It adds Section 5.5 and Appendix H while retaining the overall narrative structure.

P2.justification: v2 adds the efficiency table, merges v1 Tables 5 and 12 into Table 6, and expands Table 4 to full width. Existing figures are retained and reflowed, with limited caption edits and corresponding table renumbering.

improvement.justification: New Section 5.5 and Appendix H improve transparency about computational costs and policy-network implementation; consolidating the error analysis also improves accessibility. These useful but bounded gains are partly offset by inconsistencies in the added material: Table 5 lists 4,085 PPO parameters versus 4,805 in the prose, and Section 5.5 states 100M encoder parameters versus 110M elsewhere.
